title: Daypart allocation & fragmentation readout — weekly dashboard export
body:
OVERVIEW:
This export is a working weekly readout from the internal GPU utilization dashboard focused on daypart (hour-of-day) allocation, pool fragmentation, and short-term headroom projections across clusters/regions. Unlike the usual fleet rollups, this sheet slices utilization by cluster -> pool -> daypart and surfaces microburst risk for the next 72 hours based on trailing 7-day patterns.

Key goals:
- Surface which pools are losing effective capacity due to fragmentation (many small reservations / stranded sockets).
- Show daypart-driven contention windows where latency SLOs may breach if incoming traffic follows recent trends.
- Recommend immediate mitigations (burst routing, temporary reservations, slot condensation).

EXPORT TABLE (CSV-like):
cluster,pool,daypart,hours_sampled,gpu_hours_used,gpu_hours_total,util_pct,95th_token_latency_ms,avg_queue_len,notes
na-cluster-7,priority,08-12,28,1120,1400,80.0,18,0.2,steady morning spike from product tests
na-cluster-7,standard,08-12,28,900,2100,42.9,36,1.1,spot pre-emption events at 09:10
na-cluster-7,spot,08-12,28,160,800,20.0,120,3.8,high churn; eviction thrash
eu-west-2a,dedicated-reserved,14-18,28,980,1000,98.0,12,0.0,customer reserved pool at peak
eu-west-2a,standard,14-18,28,420,1300,32.3,45,0.9,evening regression evals
apac-gpu-05,priority,00-04,28,240,300,80.0,22,0.4,maintenance windows reduce capacity 02:00-03:00
apac-gpu-05,spot,00-04,28,30,200,15.0,150,4.6,very high fragmentation; many single-slot pods
na-cluster-3,priority,16-20,28,1400,1600,87.5,20,0.1,false-positive autoscaler flares earlier this week
na-cluster-3,standard,16-20,28,780,2200,35.5,40,1.3,queueing around 17:30 correlated with scheduled jobs

INTERPRETATION NOTES:
- High fragmentation signal in 'spot' pools (apac-gpu-05, na-cluster-7) — small allocations (<=1 GPU) account for ~62% of active spot sockets in those pools during high contention dayparts. This reduces effective capacity and increases eviction impact.
- Dedicated-reserved pools are consistently at >95% in key customer clusters (eu-west-2a). Recommend evaluating short-lived burst capacity or scheduled slot borrowing from adjacent AZs during evening window (14-18 local).
- Daypart risk windows: NA morning (08-12) and NA late afternoon (16-20) show coincident peaks across priority + standard pools; if product testing traffic repeats, tail latencies may move from current 95th=18-36ms to >50ms for standard workloads.

MICROBURST / SLO RISK ESTIMATES (72h forecast):
- na-cluster-7 (08-12): 38% chance of queueing causing >50ms token latency for standard pool if incoming ramp matches last 3 weekdays.
- na-cluster-3 (16-20): 22% chance of spillover to regional fallback due to priority oversubscription; current fallback policy would route to eu pools incurring +60ms RTT.
- apac-gpu-05 (00-04): 8% chance of degraded throughput given ongoing maintenance windows.

RECOMMENDATIONS (short-term):
1) Enable temporary slot condensation for spot pools in APAC and NA for the next 48h: consolidate single-GPU pods into contiguous sockets for 6-hour windows to reduce fragmentation impact.
2) Create a transient reservation (48h) of 200 GPU-hours in na-cluster-7 dedicated pool to cover predicted morning ramp; label as "experiment: morning-buffer-2026-12".
3) Adjust autoscaler floor for eu-west-2a dedicated-reserved pool during 14-18 to avoid preemptive downscale.
4) Add a telemetry flag to sample socket-level allocation size (1/5th of allocations) to quantify single-slot fragmentation more precisely.

ACTION ITEMS (owners & ETA):
- Priya N. (me): spin up test slot-condensation job and monitor until 2026-12-08 06:00 UTC.
- Ethan C.: open quick reservation (ops console) and notify account team (ENGINFRA-4321) by EOD 2026-12-06.
- Marta R.: update autoscaler policy PR and add canary for eu-west-2a; target merge 2026-12-07.
- SRE on-call: watch priority fallback traces for na-cluster-3 during 16-20 window next three days.

DATA QUALITY / KNOWN GAPS:
- GPU-hours_total uses cluster inventory snapshot taken at 2026-12-05 02:00 UTC; maintenance and unscheduled reboots after that time will not be reflected.
- Queue length is sampled from the routing proxy every 60s; spiky microbursts <60s can be undercounted.
- Some legacy pools still tag "pool_type" inconsistently (standard vs shared-standard); mapping applied heuristically.

QUESTIONS TO RESOLVE / FOLLOW-UPS:
- Should we prioritize consolidation (temp condensation) or short-term reservations? Cost trade-off analysis needed — quick calc shows 200 GPU-hour reservation ~ $6.5k (list price) vs operational risk of SLO breaches (hard to quantify).
- Can billing/chargeback tolerate temporary cross-pool borrowing? Legal/finance sign-off needed for customer-tagged reserved pools.

RAW EXPORT LINK: confluence://exports/gpu-daypart-2026-12-05.csv (internal only)

NOTES TO SELF / SCRATCH:
- If condensation reduces eviction rate by >40% in spot pools, consider adding condensation as an automated mitigation when fragmentation metric > 0.55.
- Potential follow-up: build a "daypart simulator" that replays request patterns against synthetic capacity to estimate microburst probability more precisely.

END OF EXPORT.
summary: Weekly working export slicing utilization by cluster/pool/daypart. Highlights fragmentation in spot pools (APAC/NA), dedicated-reserved pressure in EU, recommends short-term condensation + transient reservation and autoscaler tweaks.
